add-authzclientcryptoprovider-for-author.texto: WHAT: New abstract method int order() has no default, breaking all existing CryptoProvider implementations. WHY: Legacy providers on classpath throw AbstractMethodError when CryptoIntegration sorts by order, crashing init instead of loading. HOW: Change to default int order() { return 0; }.

WHAT: concatenatedRSToASN1DER copies signature without validating signature.length == signLength. WHY: Short/long JWS signatures throw unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of declared IOException, escaping callers that only catch IOException (ECDSASignatureVerifierContext) and causing 500/crash. HOW: Validate length first and throw IOException on mismatch.

WHAT: readSequence loops while(length>0) with length-=bytes.length and never validates exact consumption or indefinite length -1. WHY: Overlong inner TLVs drive length negative and exit silently, and 0x80 indefinite length returns empty list, producing wrong R/S split or confusing downstream size error instead of rejecting malformed DER.

WHAT: integerToBytes silently truncates oversized integers to low qLength bytes and does not reject negative BigIntegers. WHY: Invalid DER R/S values are mapped to a different valid concatenated value instead of throwing, causing wrong output and signature malleability versus strict DER validation.

WHAT: detectProvider sorts by order and silently picks first, but Default/Elytron/FIPS all return order 200 so ties fall back to nondeterministic ServiceLoader order. WHY: Classpath with both FIPS and non-FIPS providers no longer errors and can silently select non-compliant crypto, breaking FIPS compliance without warning.

WHAT: getBouncyCastleProvider returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider() instead of a BouncyCastle provider or null. WHY: Breaks the CryptoProvider contract honored by Default/FIPS (BC provider) and Elytron (null); callers expecting a BC provider get the SUN/JKS provider, causing wrong-provider crypto operations. HOW: Return null (like WildFlyElytronProvider) or throw UnsupportedOperationException consistent with other unimplemented methods.

WHAT: Single default-curve EC KeyPair generated once in constructor is reused for ES256, ES384 and ES512 tests. WHY: Default EC genKeyPair is P-256, so ES384 (96-byte) and ES512 (132-byte) conversions only exercise zero-padded P-256 signatures and never validate real P-384/P-521 signatures, giving false confidence via round-trip assert. HOW: Generate per-algorithm keypairs with explicit curve params (e.g., secp256r1/secp384r1/secp521r1) matching each ECDSAAlgorithm.

add-comprehensive-email-validation-for-b.texto: WHAT: BlockedEmail.should_block? does case-sensitive exact lookup BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first. WHY: Attacker bypasses block by changing case (e.g. FOO@bar.com vs foo@bar.com) while domain checks use case-insensitive Regexp and codebase normalizes via Email.downcase elsewhere. HOW: Normalize both sides with Email.downcase(email).strip before query (and on create).

WHAT: validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block? which mutates DB (match_count+=1, last_match_at, save) inside validation. WHY: Rails runs validations twice per create (valid? + save) so one signup attempt inflates match_count by 2 and updates last_match_at spuriously, corrupting blocked-stats. HOW: Make validation side-effect-free and increment stats once in controller/service after failed save, or guard with atomic update_counters outside validator.

WHAT: emailValidation depends on 'rejectedEmails.@each' for an array of primitive strings. WHY: @each observes properties of array items, not membership; pushObject(result.values.email) does not invalidate the computed property so the remembered rejected email error is not shown until accountEmail itself changes. HOW: Change dependent key to 'rejectedEmails.[]' (or 'rejectedEmails.length').

WHAT: EmailValidator.validate_each only checks whitelist/blacklist/blocked and never validates email syntax, while User now relies solely on validates :email, email:true for email shape. WHY: Malformed strings with no @/domain pass validation and create users with undeliverable emails, breaking mail delivery and downstream assumptions. HOW: Restore a format check (e.g. against User::EMAIL) in EmailValidator before the restriction/blocked checks.

add-groups-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.texto: WHAT: Global canManage() grants manage on VIEW scope (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)). WHY: A caller with only view/all-groups permission passes manage checks (e.g. group creation/management gates), privilege escalation from viewer to manager. HOW: Check only MANAGE scope for canManage().

WHAT: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission uses groupResource.getId() (authz resource UUID) instead of groupResource.getName() (group id) both for lookup and for the granted set. WHY: findByName(server, resource-UUID) misses the per-group resource and falls back to all-groups evaluation, and the returned set contains resource UUIDs not group IDs so downstream UserModel.GROUPS DB filtering (UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource) filters on wrong IDs and returns wrong/empty user sets. HOW: Use groupResource.getName() for hasPermission and granted.add().

WHAT: canView(user)/canManage(user) dropped AdminRoles.ADMIN from the fast-path role check present before. WHY: A master-realm ADMIN without MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS in the target realm now falls through to hasPermission which returns false when !isAdminSameRealm, denying legitimate master admins (regression). HOW: Restore ADMIN to the hasOneAdminRole checks.

WHAT: getSubGroups removed the canViewGlobal short-circuit and now calls auth.groups()::canView per subgroup (V2 does resource lookup + evaluatePermission each). WHY: For global viewers/all-groups grantees this turns one evaluation into N evaluations per page of subgroups, hot-path fanout on group listing. HOW: Restore the canViewGlobal fast path before per-group filtering.

add-rolling-updates-feature-flag-and-com.texto: WHAT: The feature-disabled guard added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run has no test coverage while the identical guard in UpdateCompatibilityMetadata is covered by testFeatureNotEnabled. WHY: Removing or breaking the Check guard would not fail any test, leaving the gated command unprotected. HOW: Add a dist-test launch of {UpdateCompatibility.NAME, UpdateCompatibilityCheck.NAME} without --features asserting the disabled error and exit code 4, mirroring the metadata case.

advanced-date-override-handling-and-time.texto: WHAT: Line 114 compares two Dayjs objects with === (reference equality) so full-day/zero-length override check never matches. WHY: Dead branch means that override case falls through to before/after checks and yields wrong available/unavailable verdict for that edge. HOW: Compare instants with .isSame(), .valueOf() or +dayjs.

WHAT: Working-hours check computes both start and end from slotStartTime (end ignores eventLength/slotEndTime). WHY: Multi-slot events that overflow workingHours.endTime are wrongly reported available (wrong output/broken contract). HOW: Compute end from slotEndTime.

WHAT: dateOverrides.find callback sets dateOverrideExist as side effect but returns truthy only when slot is outside that override, so with two overrides on the same day a slot inside override A but before override B returns true and is rejected. WHY: Splits/merges multiple same-day overrides into wrong unavailable verdict. HOW: First find matching-day override(s), then test containment without mixing overrides.

WHAT: New offset code calls .tz(override.timeZone) and .tz(timeZone) without guarding optional/unknown zones and parses via override.start.toString(). WHY: Undefined/invalid zone from optional TimeRange.timeZone or invitee input throws or yields NaN offset, crashing slot generation or shifting all override times. HOW: Guard missing zones and parse Date directly with dayjs(override.start).tz().

WHAT: Per-day per-override path builds 6+ Dayjs+tz objects (two utcOffset lookups plus hour/minute extraction via repeated utc().add(offset)). WHY: Executed inside getTimeSlots day loop so cost scales O(days*overrides) with heavy date parsing on hot availability path. HOW: Parse each override once per call and reuse start/end minutes.

WHAT: Date-override shift uses dayjs.tz(date.start, organizerTimeZone).utcOffset() * -1 then add(utcOffset), inverting the UTC-to-wall conversion (wall = UTC + offset, not UTC - offset). WHY: Day matching and start/end range checks are shifted by twice the organizer offset in the wrong direction, so slots match the wrong override day and in/out-of-override verdicts are wrong for non-UTC organizers. HOW: Remove the * -1 (add the raw utcOffset) to match the offset-difference convention used in packages/lib/slots.ts.

WHAT: Working-hours outsideness uses workingHours.find where the predicate returns true when that single entry does not contain the slot. WHY: With multiple entries for the same weekday (split shifts) a slot inside one entry still matches another non-containing entry, so find returns truthy and a valid slot is rejected as outside working hours. HOW: Invert the quantifier — return false only when no entry for that day contains the slot (e.g. check !some(entry contains slot)).

advanced-query-processing-architecture-g.texto: WHAT: Queries interpolated with applyTemplateVariables at line 299 are interpolated again downstream (DataSourceWithBackend.query re-applies applyTemplateVariables before backend, and shard path calls runSplitQuery after already interpolating). WHY: applyTemplateVariables calls addAdHocFilters, so the second/third pass re-adds the same adhocFilters to an expr that already contains them, producing duplicated labels/wrong expr. HOW: Interpolate once at the entry point and strip filters/scopedVars from sub-requests, or make downstream passes skip applyTemplateVariables/adHoc when already applied.

WHAT: New code filters empty expr before interpolation, while old code interpolated via interpolateVariablesInQueries first then filtered. WHY: A query with truthy raw expr (e.g. "$var") that interpolates to empty/falsey is now kept and sent to splitQueriesByStreamShard/shard fetching instead of being dropped, causing empty-selector fetch and invalid sub-queries. HOW: Move the .filter(query.expr) to after the .map(applyTemplateVariables) or filter on the interpolated expr.

async-import-of-the-appstore-packages-ca.texto: WHAT: getCalendarCredentials stays sync but `getCalendar(credential)` on line 28 now returns Promise<Calendar|null>, so `calendar` field stores a Promise instead of Calendar. WHY: Breaks the function's contract — callers found via grep (viewer.tsx:340,415, availability/calendar.ts:83) expecting Calendar get a Promise; only getConnectedCalendars was patched to `await item.calendar`, other uses of `.calendar` will call calendar methods on a Promise and crash/misbehave. HOW: Make getCalendarCredentials async and `await getCalendar(credential)` (or Promise.all), and update all 3 callers to await it.

WHAT: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent ...)` discards all promises — forEach never awaited. WHY: Calendar/video deletions run fire-and-forget with unobserved rejections; try/catch around forEach cannot catch async errors and reschedule email/webhook below runs before deletions complete, leaving stale bookings. HOW: Replace with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))`.

WHAT: Same `forEach(async ... await getCalendar ... return calendar?.deleteEvent)` fire-and-forget inside try/catch (identical in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts:125). WHY: Returned delete promises are discarded, async import+delete errors become unhandled rejections not caught by surrounding try/catch, and function proceeds to send reschedule email without waiting for cancellations. HOW: Use `await Promise.all(...map...)` or for..of with await.

WHAT: Recurring-booking path uses `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar ... await calendar?.deleteEvent; apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) })` without awaiting the forEach. WHY: Pushes into apiDeletes happen after async suspend, so outer code awaiting apiDeletes races the loop — deletes can be missed entirely and errors uncaught. HOW: Collect with `map` + `await Promise.all` or for..of with await before pushing.

WHAT: `getVideoAdapters` awaits each dynamic `import()` sequentially in `for (const cred of withCredentials) { await appStore[...] }`. WHY: N credentials cause N serial import resolutions instead of parallel, adding linear latency to every availability/meeting call (same pattern in handleCancelBooking.ts:480-482 for..of with await getCalendar). HOW: Resolve in parallel with `Promise.all(withCredentials.map(...))`.

authzservice-improve-authz-caching-grafa.texto: WHAT: Check returns Allowed:true directly from stale permCache without DB revalidation. WHY: A permission revoked after the cache entry was written still authorizes for up to shortCacheTTL (30s), creating a privilege-revocation bypass window that did not exist when Check always queried the DB. HOW: Revalidate revocations before trusting cached allow, or shorten/invalidate permCache on permission changes.

WHAT: List serves whatever scopeMap is in permCache without the per-item DB fallback that Check has. WHY: Newly granted dashboards/folders stay invisible (and revoked ones stay listed) until permCache TTL expires, regressing List from always-fresh getIdentityPermissions to stale reads and contradicting the PR goal. HOW: Apply the same miss/outdated fallback for List or bypass permCache for List.

WHAT: Check short-circuits to deny on permDenialCache hit without requerying permissions. WHY: A denial cached at line 154 is never cleared when permissions are later granted, so a newly granted resource is still denied until shortCacheTTL expiry, reintroducing the staleness the cached-perms fallback was meant to fix. HOW: Invalidate/delete the denial key when fresh permissions grant the resource, or do not short-circuit and always attempt the cached-perms then DB fallback.

WHAT: Every denied Check inserts a distinct denial entry keyed by (namespace,user,action,name,parent) via userPermDenialCacheKey. WHY: Name/parent are request-controlled with unbounded cardinality, so enumerating random resources fills the shared cache with single-use denial keys until expiry, growing memory and evicting useful entries. HOW: Bound denial-cache cardinality (e.g. only cache denies for known resources, limit size, or use a negative cache with coarse keys).

comprehensive-workflow-reminder-manageme.texto: WHAT: immediateDelete path POSTs cancel to SendGrid then returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row. WHY: Leaves an orphan scheduled=true row after workflow/step delete and reschedule callers (workflows.tsx:214,521 handleNewBooking.ts:968) so DB claims scheduled while SendGrid is cancelled. HOW: Delete the prisma row after successful cancel when immediateDelete is true.

WHAT: for-loop awaits SendGrid cancel per reminder and only after the loop awaits collected deletes; any throw jumps to catch and skips Promise.all. WHY: Single SendGrid failure aborts remaining cancels and discards already-queued deletes so cancelled emails are neither cancelled nor cleaned up. HOW: Per-reminder try/catch with finally-awaited deletes or Promise.allSettled.

WHAT: forEach calls async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without await and results are not added to prismaPromises. WHY: Handler returns before cancelled=true/delete persists and async errors are swallowed inside managers, so cancelled bookings can still send reminders. HOW: Collect promises and await Promise.all.

WHAT: try/catch wraps forEach of async deletes without await. WHY: forEach does not propagate async rejections so catch never fires and cancellations run fire-and-forget during reschedule, leaving old reminders active. HOW: Use for..of with await or Promise.all inside try.

WHAT: Awaited SendGrid cancel inside for..of over remindersToCancel issues N sequential network calls. WHY: Cron latency grows O(N) with cancelled-reminder count, delaying the 72h scheduling pass below. HOW: Fire cancels concurrently with Promise.all/pool.

WHAT: deleteScheduledSMSReminder now awaits twilio.cancelSMS before the prisma delete in the same try block, so a Twilio failure skips the DB delete. WHY: Previously the caller deleted the reminder row independently even when the Twilio cancel threw (manager swallowed), but now a transient Twilio error leaves a scheduled SMS row with no cancelled flag and no retry, so the SMS is still sent for a cancelled/rescheduled booking. HOW: Delete the row independently of Twilio result (or mark cancelled and retry), e.g. move the prisma delete outside the Twilio try or into a finally.

database-performance-optimizations-grafa.texto: WHAT: Leftover debug r.log.Error on every cleanup batch logs full ids slice, cond and nil err (lines 534,537,554,557,576,579). WHY: Error-level spam on hot path with up to batchSize IDs (32767 in test) blows up logs/disk and formatting cost every minute. HOW: Demote to Debug and drop ids/cond payload or cap length.

WHAT: untilDoneOrCancelled stops when RowsAffected==0 instead of when fetched IDs are empty. WHY: With split fetch-then-delete, fetched IDs can vanish before delete (concurrent cleanup/insert-delete race), returning 0 affected while many rows remain, causing premature termination and under-delete beyond the documented tolerance. HOW: Return/stop on len(ids)==0 from fetch, not on affected==0.

WHAT: Global cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. WHY: Runs all cleanup jobs (snapshots, versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history, annotations) 10x more often, multiplying DB/IO load with no justification in PR. HOW: Revert to 10 minutes or gate faster cadence behind annotation-only job/config.

enhanced-pagination-performance-for-high.texto: WHAT: BasePaginator.get_result clamps negative offset to 0 for forward cursors but passes it through for is_prev cursors (start_offset = max(0,offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset). WHY: Inconsistent handling returns first page for crafted forward negative cursor instead of error and still passes negative start to queryset[offset:stop] for prev cursors where Django forbids negative indexing (AssertionError/500) plus line 192 length check uses raw offset causing wrong trim.

WHAT: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key does int(math.floor/ceil(value)) and value_from_cursor returns raw cursor.value, copying integer-id Paginator semantics instead of DateTimePaginator datetime conversion. WHY: Caller passes order_by='-datetime' (organization_auditlogs.py:80) so getattr returns datetime which crashes math.floor with TypeError and datetime-column filtering with int cursor_value produces wrong results/DB error — broken paginator contract.

WHAT: OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features allows attacker-controlled cursor.offset<0 to reach queryset[start_offset:stop] with negative start, falsely claimed safe because Django handles it and permissions are at queryset level. WHY: Cursor offset is parsed from user-supplied ?cursor= string with no negative validation (Cursor.__init__ just int(offset)); crafted negative offset triggers unhandled AssertionError (DoS/500) or out-of-bounds pagination window bypass, reachable via ?optimized_pagination=true gated only on has_global_access.

WHAT: Changed line 71 dereferences organization_context.member.has_global_access without a None check though member is Optional. WHY: A request reaching get() with member=None and request.user.is_superuser falsy raises AttributeError and returns 500 instead of a paginated response. HOW: Guard with (organization_context.member is not None and organization_context.member.has_global_access).

feat-add-calendar-cache-status-and-actio.texto: WHAT: updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data {} so no column is set despite the comment claiming to bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. WHY: Prisma updateMany with no data is a validation error/no-op, aborting or wasting the post-cache-warm touch and leaving the cache-status timestamp stale. HOW: Pass an explicit touch field e.g. updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, { updatedAt: new Date() }).

WHAT: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars while disconnectMutation does (onSettled invalidate). WHY: After deleting cache the enriched cacheUpdatedAt stays cached in the tRPC query so the dropdown keeps showing the old Last updated timestamp until manual reload. HOW: Mirror disconnect logic — await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate() in deleteCache onSuccess/onSettled.

WHAT: sed -i '' -E uses BSD/macOS in-place syntax. WHY: Fails on GNU/Linux (sed: can't read : No such file or directory) so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated on Linux dev machines. HOW: Branch on uname or use a portable update (e.g. sed -i.bak / awk / perl -pi -e).

WHAT: ENV_FILE="../.env" is resolved against the caller's CWD, not the script location. WHY: Running from repo root vs scripts/ writes/creates the wrong .env (or parent-dir .env), silently misconfiguring GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. HOW: Resolve relative to the script dir, e.g. SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd); ENV_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/../.env".

feat-upsampling-support-upsampled-error-.texto: WHAT: Errors-dataset queries are enabled for upsampling but upsampled_count is only registered on DiscoverDatasetConfig. WHY: Errors-dataset timeseries/top-events calls will resolve an unknown function and fail or fall back incorrectly when allowlisted. HOW: Register upsampled_count for the errors dataset config too, or gate errors dataset off until supported.

WHAT: _is_error_focused_query uses substring 'event.type:error in query' to gate discover upsampling. WHY: A mixed discover query such as 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction' matches and upsample-sums transaction rows by sample_weight, inflating non-error counts. HOW: Parse the query AST for event.type equality instead of substring matching, or require error-only filter.

WHAT: transform only rewrites exact 'count()' and emits hardcoded 'upsampled_count() as count'. WHY: Aliased/parameterized forms ('count() as foo', 'count(x)', whitespace variants), equations, and orderby referencing count() are left unrewritten or mis-aliased, yielding raw instead of upsampled numbers and mismatched top-N ordering. HOW: Preserve the original alias/expression structure when rewriting and also rewrite equations/orderby references.

WHAT: upsampled_count wraps sum(ifNull(sample_weight,1)) in toInt64 truncation. WHY: Fractional weights/sums are floored (e.g. 9.99 becomes 9), systematically undercounting upsampled totals versus rounding. HOW: Use round() before toInt64 or return the float sum directly.

feat-uptime-add-ability-to-use-queues-to.texto: WHAT: _get_partition_lock creates per-partition locks via unsynchronized get+setdefault on partition_locks dict. WHY: concurrent add_offset (submit thread) and complete_offset/get_committable (worker/commit threads) for a new Partition can create two different Lock objects and mutate all_offsets/outstanding dict structure without protection, breaking the claimed thread-safety and risking lost updates or RuntimeError during list(all_offsets.keys()). HOW: guard lock creation/all_offsets structure mutation with a global lock.

WHAT: OrderedQueueWorker.complete_offset is called in finally even when result_processor failed, and ResultProcessor.__call__ itself swallows exceptions. WHY: failed uptime results are marked completed so get_committable_offsets advances past them and the commit loop commits them, silently dropping failed checks with no retry/DLQ despite docstring claiming only successful processing is committed.

WHAT: SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close/terminate shuts down the factory-shared FixedQueuePool, and each create_with_partitions spawns a new commit thread sharing the same OffsetTracker. WHY: on rebalance/second create_with_partitions the old strategy's close kills the shared pool for the new strategy (puts raise ShutDown, offsets leak) or leaves multiple commit threads calling stale commit callbacks.

WHAT: close() sets shutdown_event and joins the commit thread before draining workers. WHY: offsets that complete after the commit thread exits are never committed (final tail lost), causing duplicate reprocessing on restart; shutdown must drain workers first then do a final commit.

WHAT: FixedQueuePool creates unbounded queue.Queue() with no maxsize and OffsetTracker retains every offset until the head completes. WHY: a single slow group blocks the contiguous commit point so all_offsets/outstanding grow without bound while the producer never blocks, causing memory exhaustion and an O(range) scan in get_committable_offsets every second.

WHAT: OrderedQueueWorker.run checks `while not self.shutdown` so FixedQueuePool.shutdown setting worker.shutdown=True makes workers exit after the current item instead of draining remaining queued WorkItems until queue.ShutDown. WHY: queued items are abandoned on every graceful shutdown (offsets never completed/committed, forcing replay and delaying shutdown semantics that immediate=False explicitly requested). HOW: loop until ShutDown (e.g. `while True` with break only on queue.ShutDown) and use the flag only to unblock or skip re-queuing, not to abort the drain.

feature-per-topic-unsubscribe-option-in-.texto: WHAT: TopicUser.find_by can return nil and then tu.notification_level is dereferenced without a guard. WHY: Causes NoMethodError 500 for users with no TopicUser row for the topic (also crashes if notification_level is nil since nil > Integer raises). HOW: Handle nil e.g. initialize via TopicUser.get/change or create the row before downgrading.

WHAT: GET topics#unsubscribe performs a state-changing mutation (downgrades TopicUser.notification_level and save!) with no CSRF protection. WHY: Allows cross-site/preview-prefetch triggered unsubscribes since GETs are not CSRF-guarded and email scanners/link prefetchers will fire the URL.

WHAT: Topic#unsubscribe_url returns a relative path interpolated into email markdown via user_notifications.rb unsubscribe_url. WHY: Email clients cannot resolve a relative href so the per-topic unsubscribe link in notification emails is broken.

WHAT: Shared unsubscribe_link translation now requires %{unsubscribe_url} but other senders using add_unsubscribe_link do not supply it. WHY: Raises I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument or renders a broken link for every other email type that uses the unsubscribe footer.

WHAT: New topicUnsubscribe route at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe collides with existing topic.fromParamsNear /:nearPost route which matches any string including 'unsubscribe'. WHY: Navigation to the unsubscribe URL can resolve to the topic post-stream route with nearPost='unsubscribe' instead of the unsubscribe template, loading the wrong page and feeding a non-numeric nearPost into closestPostForPostNumber/refresh logic. HOW: Define the unsubscribe route before the topic resource, constrain :nearPost to numeric/last, or use a distinct path that cannot match :nearPost.

implement-recovery-key-support-for-user-.texto: WHAT: New getCredentials() dereferences myUser without a null check (myUser.recoveryCodes). WHY: Throws NPE for unknown/removed users during federated credential lookup, crashing authentication where sibling methods (isConfiguredFor, getDisableableCredentialTypesStream) explicitly null-guard. HOW: Return Stream.empty() when getMyUser(user) is null before touching fields.

WHAT: Changed lookup now returns federated recovery credentials via RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential, but exhaustion cleanup still calls removeStoredCredentialById which only deletes from the local store. WHY: An exhausted federated recovery-codes credential is never removed (local delete misses the federated id), leaving stale all-used credentials and forcing repeated re-configuration instead of clean rotation.

WHAT: Federated recovery codes are stored as raw JSON via updateCredential with no consumption/invalidation wiring, unlike the local path where RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid removes the used code and calls updateStoredCredential. WHY: A federated validator that only checks equality (as the PR reference impl does with anyMatch) re-accepts an already-used recovery code indefinitely, allowing replay of single-use backup codes.

optimize-spans-buffer-insertion-with-evi.texto: WHAT: Changed SADD/SSCAN to ZADD/ZSCAN with no migration breaks existing Redis keys of Set type. WHY: Redis raises WRONGTYPE when ZADD/ZCARD/ZSCAN/ZUNIONSTORE hits a pre-deploy Set key (TTL up to 3600s), failing process_spans/flush during rollout. HOW: Handle WRONGTYPE/migrate (e.g., DEL or convert old sets) or version the key.

WHAT: Direct val["end_timestamp_precise"] raises KeyError when the field is absent. WHY: One old/malformed SpanEvent crashes the whole process_batch batch instead of skipping/defaulting. HOW: Use val.get("end_timestamp_precise") with a fallback (e.g., now/timestamp) or validate and drop the span.

WHAT: ZUNIONSTORE uses default AGGREGATE SUM so a duplicate payload member gets score+score. WHY: Retried/reprocessed spans double their end_timestamp (~3.4e9), corrupting order so duplicates become unevictable and wrong spans are evicted via ZPOPMIN. HOW: Add "AGGREGATE", "MAX" to both ZUNIONSTORE calls.

WHAT: Redirect-chase limit cut from 10000 to 1000 with no functional need. WHY: Segment trees with redirect chains deeper than 1000 stop resolving early and spans are joined into the wrong set, silently splitting/corrupting segments. HOW: Restore 10000 limit or keep eviction cap (1000 spans) separate from traversal depth.

WHAT: ZPOPMIN eviction by lowest end_timestamp can evict the segment/root span payload while hrs flag stays "1". WHY: Downstream flush then emits a segment marked has-root without the root span, producing a corrupt segment. HOW: Protect the segment span from eviction or clear/adjust hrs handling when it is evicted.

WHAT: Flush path removed the max_segment_spans span-count guard, leaving max_segment_spans config dead. WHY: Any segment bypassing Lua eviction (legacy sets, races, future callers) is now flushed unbounded instead of skipped, breaking downstream size assumptions. HOW: Re-add a span-count check after ZSCAN pagination or explicitly wire max_segment_spans to the Lua cap.

scale-color-lightness-must-use-secondary.texto: WHAT: Light-theme branch uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) while original was $lightness: 70%. WHY: Changes light-theme color for .custom-message-length instead of preserving it; desktop/modal.scss correctly preserves 70%/30%. HOW: Change first arg back to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%).

WHAT: .topic-meta-data h5 a light branch uses $lightness: 70% while original was $lightness: 30%. WHY: Inverts light-theme color and breaks intent to preserve light appearance; arguments appear swapped (70%/30% instead of 30%/70%). HOW: Change to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)).

WHAT: .topic-map h3 light branch uses $lightness: 50% while original was $lightness: 20%. WHY: Shifts light-theme heading color lighter; desktop/topic-post.scss correctly preserves 20%/80% for same selector. HOW: Change to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%)).

WHAT: .group-member-info .name light branch uses $lightness: 50% while original was $lightness: 30%. WHY: Lightens light-theme name color vs original; common/base/user.scss preserves 30%/70% for .name. HOW: Change first arg back to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) with dark complement 70%.

WHAT: .group-member-info .name light branch uses $lightness: 50% while original was $lightness: 30%. WHY: Same light-theme regression as desktop/user.scss duplicate; diverges from common/base/user.scss 30%/70%.
