ux-show-complete-url-path-if-website-dom.texto: WHAT: Conditional include method is named include_website_name without trailing ? while AMS and all sibling predicates use include_<attr>? . WHY: The serializer framework never calls the misnamed predicate so website_name is always serialized (or never correctly gated), breaking the website.present? contract. HOW: Rename to def include_website_name? to match convention.

WHAT: Same-domain website_name is built as website_host + URI(website).path, dropping query string, fragment, and port (and not normalizing case). WHY: A same-domain URL like http://example.com/user?tab=about#bio displays as example.com/user, losing the distinguishing path and showing wrong/truncated output contrary to complete-path intent.

WHAT: The same-domain check only matches when the website host is the parent of the instance host, so a website that is a subdomain of the instance never shows its path. WHY: Line 149 tests discourse_host.ends_with?(website_host), which is false when website_host is longer (e.g. website forum.example.com with instance example.com), so it returns bare host and drops the distinguishing path. HOW: Also match the reverse direction, e.g. website_host.ends_with?("." + discourse_host), before falling back to bare host.

add-caching-support-for-identityprovider.texto: WHAT: New getForLogin cache has no invalidation on removeAll() (which only invalidates the count key). WHY: After removeAll the cached IdentityProviderListQuery per FetchMode still returns the old internalIds, serving deleted brokers as login options until natural eviction. HOW: Call registerIDPLoginInvalidation-equivalent (invalidate all FetchMode login keys) in removeAll().

WHAT: New getLoginPredicate() clause dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) without null-guarding getConfig(). WHY: A programmatically built IdentityProviderModel with null config (or null config map from storage) throws NPE in every getForLogin/invalidation path that evaluates the predicate, breaking login rendering. HOW: Null-guard the config map before get(), e.g. idp.getConfig() != null && Boolean.parseBoolean(...).

WHAT: Cache miss for a new organizationId calls cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey), evicting all already-cached org searches for that FetchMode cluster-wide. WHY: Each distinct org login view invalidates and rewrites the shared per-mode entry, causing cache thrashing and redundant idpDelegate.getForLogin DB loads that grow with organization count. HOW: Merge the new searchKey without a full invalidate (revisioned put), mirroring append-only semantics.

WHAT: The new getForLogin cache (key realmId+.idp.login.+mode, per-org searchKeys) is never invalidated when an IDP is linked/unlinked to an organization via OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider. WHY: Those methods (InfinispanOrganizationProvider:250-270) only register organization invalidation, so cached REALM_ONLY/ORG_ONLY/ALL ID sets stay stale — a newly linked IDP still appears in REALM_ONLY and is missing from ORG_ONLY (and vice-versa on unlink), showing wrong login brokers. HOW: Invalidate all FetchMode login keys for the realm when organization-IDP membership changes (or hook registerIDPLoginInvalidation into the organization provider path).

add-client-resource-type-and-scopes-to-a.texto: WHAT: resourceStore.findByName passes server.getId() as ownerId instead of server.getClientId(). WHY: Resources are created with owner resourceServer.getClientId() (AdminPermissionsSchema:104) and the default finder uses getClientId(), so the 3-arg lookup never matches and per-client permissions are never found, forcing incorrect fallback to all-clients. HOW: Pass server.getClientId() or use the 2-arg findByName overload like UserPermissionsV2 does.

WHAT: Fallback path does not null-check getResourceTypeResource before findByResource. WHY: getResourceTypeResource returns null when the Clients type resource is missing, so findByResource(server, null) throws NPE; the sibling hasPermission(String) overload correctly returns false on null. HOW: Add if (resource == null) return false before the findByResource check.

WHAT: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of returning boolean. WHY: Caller AbstractTokenExchangeProvider expects a boolean deny/allow and will propagate 500 on every token-exchange when V2 is enabled, breaking the contract that V1 satisfies by returning false. HOW: Return false (or implement V2 evaluation) instead of throwing.

WHAT: setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException but AdminPermissions.registerListener still calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled on ClientRemovedEvent. WHY: Deleting any client when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 routes management() to MgmtPermissionsV2 will throw from the event listener and fail client removal. HOW: Guard the listener for V2 or make V2 setPermissionsEnabled a no-op.

WHAT: hasPermission accepts any returned Permission scope without checking permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()). WHY: UserPermissionsV2 filters by resourceId, but this code grants if any evaluated permission contains the scope, so a grant attached to a different resource evaluated together (typed/all-clients resource via DefaultPolicyEvaluator) can authorize the wrong client — authorization bypass. HOW: Filter by resource id like UserPermissionsV2 does, while still allowing the type-resource grant when intended.

WHAT: getClientsWithPermission calls evaluatePermission once per client resource inside findByType iteration. WHY: Client listing/filtering therefore costs O(N) full policy evaluations where N is the number of client resources in the realm, a material slowdown on large realms. HOW: Batch evaluation or query policies/scopes without per-resource full evaluation if possible.

WHAT: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() checks only VIEW (canViewClientDefault || hasPermission(VIEW)) and ignores global MANAGE. WHY: A caller granted only MANAGE on all-clients gets canManage()==true but canView()==false/canList()==false, so list/view-all is denied despite manage rights, inconsistent with canView(ClientScopeModel) which checks VIEW||MANAGE and with V1 where MANAGE_CLIENTS implies view. HOW: Add || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) to canView() (or delegate to canManage()).

WHAT: getClientsWithPermission() adds resource.getName() for every resource of type Clients, including the all-clients type resource ('Clients') itself. WHY: The returned set then contains 'Clients' which is not a client UUID, and caller AvailableRoleMappingResource.getRoleIdsWithPermissions() does realm.getClientById(cid).getRolesStream() causing null-dereference/wrong results when global permission is granted. HOW: Skip the resource whose name equals AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE (or whose id equals the type-resource id).

add-guest-management-functionality-to-ex.texto: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && instead of ||. WHY: requires caller to be both admin and owner simultaneously so legitimate team admins (non-owners) and owners (non-admins) are denied with FORBIDDEN, breaking the intended allow-either contract. HOW: change && to ||.

WHAT: any attendee whose email matches ctx user is authorized to add arbitrary guests. WHY: lets a low-privilege attendee inject unlimited emails into any booking they attend, triggering calendar updates and invite emails containing meeting/video details to attacker-chosen addresses (spam-relay / unwanted-participant abuse). HOW: restrict to organizer/team roles or require organizer approval.

WHAT: blacklist check lowercases the env list but compares raw guest (blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)) and duplicate check uses case-sensitive guest === attendee.email with no intra-request dedup. WHY: bypass via case variation (Foo@x.com vs foo@x.com) creates duplicate Attendee rows and evades BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS block. HOW: normalize with toLowerCase().trim() on both sides and dedupe uniqueGuests.

WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) passes the raw input instead of filtered uniqueGuests. WHY: existing/duplicated/blacklisted addresses filtered from the DB write are still treated as new guests for email routing (newGuests.includes branch), sending AttendeeScheduledEmail to wrong recipients and AddGuests notice to wrong set. HOW: pass uniqueGuests.

WHAT: addGuestsMutation onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but never resets isInvalidEmail. WHY: after one validation failure the red emails_must_be_unique_valid banner persists across success/close and shows stale on next open. HOW: call setIsInvalidEmail(false) in onSuccess.

WHAT: guests is unbounded z.array(z.string().email()) with no max length. WHY: single request can force createMany with thousands of rows plus per-attendee getTranslation loads and per-attendee sendEmail fanout plus calendar update, enabling DB/IO/email resource exhaustion. HOW: add .max(e.g. 10-25) and enforce server-side.

WHAT: handleAdd validates raw multiEmailValue including empty placeholder rows (initialized as [""] and appended by Add-another). WHY: any untouched empty row fails the z.string().email() check, so adding multiple guests with a blank row rejects otherwise-valid emails. HOW: filter out empty/whitespace entries before safeParse and mutate, e.g. const emails = multiEmailValue.filter((e) => e.trim() !== "").

add-html-sanitizer-for-translated-messag.texto: WHAT: Prefix/suffix trimming computes start and end independently with no overlap guard before substring. WHY: When sanitized and value share overlapping prefix/suffix (sanitizer normalizes tags, adds/removes markup) start can exceed value.length()-end, throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and aborting verification. HOW: Cap end so start+end <= min lengths, e.g. limit end search to len-start.

WHAT: santizeAnchors only iterates anchors found in the translation and never checks for English anchors missing from it, and continues iterating a stale matcher after mutating value via replaceFirst. WHY: A translation that drops an opening or closing <a> tag passes silently (returned value has anchors stripped, later HTML check sees no tags), breaking links without a verifier error and mis-attributing subsequent matches.

WHAT: santizeAnchors error message omits the key and file while the Illegal HTML message includes them. WHY: In a multi-file verifier run the anchor failure is unactionable — the offending key/file cannot be identified from the message. HOW: Include key and file in the message like the Illegal HTML branch does.

WHAT: verifySafeHtml wraps bundle-read IOExceptions in unchecked RuntimeException instead of the declared MojoExecutionException. WHY: Callers of verify() handle MojoExecutionException, so a missing/unreadable bundle or English counterpart escapes as an unhandled crash with stack trace instead of a clean Maven verification failure.

anonymous-add-configurable-device-limit-.texto: WHAT: CountDevices check-then-insert in CreateOrUpdateDevice is not atomic, so concurrent requests both see count < limit and both insert. WHY: Bypasses the device limit under concurrent anonymous logins and over-counts the table. HOW: Enforce the limit atomically (e.g. unique constraint + conditional insert, single transaction with lock, or treat rowsAffected/conflict as the limiter) instead of separate count then write.

WHAT: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before the DB write and TagDevice returns the DB error without evicting that cache entry, so a device rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached succeeds on retry via localCache hit. WHY: The new sync deny path is bypassed within the 29m cache TTL, defeating the limit. HOW: Only SetDefault after successful CreateOrUpdateDevice, or delete the cache key when CreateOrUpdateDevice returns an error.

WHAT: updateDevice restricts the UPDATE with WHERE updated_at BETWEEN [now-30d, now+1m], so an existing device whose row went stale (>30d) matches 0 rows and is misreported as ErrDeviceLimitReached. WHY: A known device cannot re-register once expired when the table is at limit, diverging from the upsert path used when under limit. HOW: Match only on device_id for existing devices (update regardless of updated_at age), and return limit-reached only when the device_id truly does not exist.

WHAT: Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously on the request context, adding CountDevices + Insert/Update DB round-trips to every anonymous login. WHY: Previously fire-and-forget with background context/timeout; now anon auth latency and availability depend on DB speed, blocking the hot auth path. HOW: Restore async tagging or gate the count/insert off the critical path when the device is already cached.

WHAT: Any unauthenticated caller can mint arbitrary X-Grafana-Device-Id values to fill the anon_device table up to the limit, after which legitimate anonymous users are denied (return nil, ErrDeviceLimitReached). WHY: Device IDs are attacker-controlled with no per-IP rate limit, proof-of-work, or privileged cleanup, enabling an anonymous slot-exhaustion DoS on anon login. HOW: Rate-limit device creation per IP, require a valid existing device for deny decisions, or fail-open with throttling instead of hard deny.

WHAT: ProvideAnonDBStore now requires a deviceLimit int64 parameter but pkg/server/wire.go:374 still registers it as a wire provider with no int64 binding. WHY: Wire cannot inject a primitive int64, so generation/build breaks or creates a duplicate store with an unresolved limit; the service now builds the store manually in impl.go:43 making the wire provider stale. HOW: Remove anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore (and its AnonStore binding if unused) from the wire set or provide a named int64/cfg-derived constructor.

WHAT: anonymousDeviceLimit is declared as `= undefined` with no type annotation while GrafanaConfig requires `number | undefined`. WHY: The property infers type `undefined` only (cf. loginError which annotates `string | undefined`), so assigning the numeric backend value fails type-checking/leaves the frontend limit unusable. HOW: Declare `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined;`.

dual-storage-architecture-grafana-codex.texto: WHAT: Update reuses the original objInfo for the async legacy write instead of pinning the storage result with updateWrapper. WHY: objInfo.UpdatedObject is re-invoked against the legacy old object and may be one-shot/stateful, so legacy gets a different/failed object and stores diverge. HOW: Restore the old pattern: wrap as &updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: res} for the legacy call.

WHAT: Async legacy writes (create/delete/update/delete-collection) derive context.WithTimeoutCause from the request ctx which is cancelled when the handler returns. WHY: The fire-and-forget goroutine is aborted by parent cancellation, so the legacy safe-measure write rarely completes and stores diverge. HOW: Detach with context.WithoutCancel(ctx) before applying the 10s timeout.

WHAT: Create passes the original input obj to Legacy.Create instead of the storage-returned created object while sharing the same mutable pointer across a goroutine. WHY: Storage-assigned defaults/resourceVersion are lost in legacy and concurrent mutation/access is a data race. HOW: Pass created (or a deep copy of it) to the legacy goroutine.

WHAT: Delete returns early on any Storage error including NotFound and skips the legacy delete; old code continued to legacy on IsNotFound. WHY: Objects existing only in legacy are never cleaned up, leaving orphan legacy copies and breaking the safe-measure invariant. HOW: Restore NotFound tolerance: attempt Legacy.Delete even when Storage returns IsNotFound.

WHAT: DeleteCollection legacy path calls recordStorageDuration for the legacy measurement, and Create/Update error paths call recordLegacyDuration for storage failures. WHY: Metrics are recorded to the wrong histogram, hiding storage vs legacy failures and breaking alerts/dashboards. HOW: Swap to recordLegacyDuration in DeleteCollection goroutine and recordStorageDuration on storage error paths.

WHAT: Delete success records the object name in the kind label position (recordStorageDuration with name). WHY: Every distinct object name creates a new Prometheus series, causing unbounded cardinality/memory blowup. HOW: Pass options.Kind like the other paths.

WHAT: Create/Get/List/Delete/Update dereference options.Kind (and List/DeleteCollection deref listOptions) without nil check. WHY: A nil options call that previously succeeded now panics with nil dereference. HOW: Guard nil options/listOptions before WithValues or default the kind label.

WHAT: Delete puts d.Log instead of the per-request log into klog.NewContext, dropping name/kind/method fields. WHY: Request-scoped log correlation for deletes is lost while all sibling methods propagate it, breaking tracing/debugging for that path. HOW: Change klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) to klog.NewContext(ctx, log).

enhance-embed-url-handling-and-validatio.texto: WHAT: attacker-controlled request.referer is interpolated unescaped into a single-quoted JS string. WHY: a Referer containing ' or </script> breaks out and executes as reflected XSS in the Discourse origin inside the framed page. HOW: encode with escape_javascript/to_json and use only the origin.

WHAT: parent.postMessage uses full request.referer as targetOrigin instead of the origin. WHY: targetOrigin must be scheme://host[:port] or *, so a full URL with path never matches and resize messages are silently dropped. HOW: pass request.protocol+host / origin only.

WHAT: url is interpolated unescaped into stored raw_html as #{url} after only a /^https?/ prefix check. WHY: a feed link or user-supplied embed_url like http://host/'> passes the check, is stored as raw_html and later rendered with raw post.cooked, giving stored XSS. HOW: HTML-escape url and quote/validate the attribute.

WHAT: cook returns raw unsanitized when cook_method is raw_html, skipping the sanitize/cooking pipeline. WHY: RSS/readability HTML from external sites is then rendered via raw post.cooked in embed/best, so any <script>/on* payload in the feed executes on the Discourse origin. HOW: sanitize raw_html through the whitelist sanitizer before storing/rendering.

WHAT: i.content.scrub assumes every feed item has content. WHY: items with only description/link have nil content, so nil.scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole hourly poll. HOW: fallback like (i.content || i.description).to_s.scrub.

WHAT: code dereferences document.getElementById('discourse-comments') without a null check before appendChild. WHY: pages missing that container throw and abort the embed script. HOW: return early if comments is null.

WHAT: origin check is reversed as discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)===-1 instead of comparing origins. WHY: any e.origin that is a substring/prefix of discourseUrl passes, letting a spoofed message drive iframe height and any future message handling. HOW: strictly compare e.origin to the expected Discourse origin.

WHAT: poll_feed loops over all rss.items with a DB lookup plus PostCreator/PostRevisor transaction per item and no limit. WHY: a large feed retriggered hourly (and synchronously from TopicRetriever) causes unbounded hourly write/query blowup and job timeouts. HOW: limit items, order newest-first with early break on unchanged sha.

WHAT: embed.post is dereferenced without a nil guard in the update branch (PostRevisor.new(post)). WHY: if the post was deleted the embed row remains so post is nil and revise! raises NoMethodError, crashing poll/retrieve and leaving content_sha1 stale. HOW: bail out or recreate when post is blank before revising.

WHAT: spec expects EmbedController#best to call TopicRetriever.new/retrieve directly while the controller enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic). WHY: the mock expectation is never satisfied so the newly added test fails and does not cover the actual async path. HOW: expect Jobs.enqueue with embed_url instead of TopicRetriever.new.

feat-2fa-backup-codes-cal-com.texto: WHAT: The new backup-code branch authenticates without verifying the password when totpCode is also present (password is only checked when `!credentials.totpCode`). WHY: An attacker knowing only email + a backup code can log in without the password by also sending a dummy totpCode, bypassing password verification. HOW: Always verify the password before either second-factor branch, independent of totpCode/backupCode presence.

WHAT: `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` and `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll` run without validation/try-catch on stored and request values. WHY: Corrupted backupCodes (rotation/decrypt failure) or non-string backupCode throws an unhandled exception, returning 500 instead of a typed error and leaving 2FA undisablable (lockout).

WHAT: handleEnable success now only does `setStep(DisplayBackupCodes)` and defers `onEnable()/resetState()` to the Close button. WHY: Dismissing via Dialog onOpenChange/Escape skips onEnable, so 2FA is enabled server-side but UI stays unchecked and the just-generated backup codes are never acknowledged/lost.

feat-ecosystem-implement-cross-system-is.texto: WHAT: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates once at import time so every AssignmentSource shares the same timestamp. WHY: Stale/shared queued breaks ordering/TTL use and makes to_dict carry incorrect time for all instances. HOW: Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead of a call-time default.

WHAT: Base `IssueSyncIntegration.sync_status_outbound` adds `assignment_source` kwarg but the `ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound(self, external_issue, is_resolved, project_id)` override accepts no **kwargs and no status-path caller was updated to thread it. WHY: Calling the override via the new base contract with assignment_source raises TypeError, and status sync cycles remain unfiltered because the param is always None.

feat-workflow-engine-add-in-hook-for-pro.texto: WHAT: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data) and remains abstract. WHY: Instantiating it via Detector.detector_handler (group_type.detector_handler(self)) raises TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class, crashing process_detectors for metric-alert detectors. HOW: Add stub implementations of the required abstract methods/properties or revert to DetectorHandler until the stateful implementation exists.

feature-automatically-downsize-large-ima.texto: WHAT: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition — 4-arg version at line 145 is immediately overridden by 3-arg version at line 149 (Ruby last-def wins), so old signature is dead. WHY: Existing caller `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` at app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 calls `downsize(path,path,100,100,opts)` which now binds as dimensions=100, opts=100, producing wrong `-resize 100\>` geometry and losing allow_animation/force_aspect_ratio — broken thumbnails or ArgumentError. HOW: Keep both arities (e.g. rename new overload or use splat/optional args) and update all callers.

WHAT: Downsize loop passes percentage geometry `"80%"` to `downsize_instructions` which appends `\>`/`\!` (yields `80%\>`) and to animated path `resize_instructions_animated` (`gifsicle --resize-fit`) which expects `WxH`. WHY: Produces invalid/unexpected geometry — convert/gifsicle fails or mis-resizes, return value ignored so loop burns 5 attempts then uploads oversized/corrupt file. HOW: Pass `WxH` dimensions (e.g. compute from FastImage) or add explicit percent handling without `\>` suffix and check return value.

WHAT: Client check hardcodes `10*1024` KB instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb']`, ignoring per-type (image vs attachment) admin limits (same hardcode at line 246 for 413 handler). WHY: If admin configures limit <10MB oversized attachments are attempted and waste upload/bandwidth only to be rejected by Validators::UploadValidator; if configured >10MB legitimate uploads are client-blocked — broken client/server contract. HOW: Restore SiteSettings lookup, or use max(10MB, configured) only for images eligible for auto-downsize.

WHAT: API URL download cap changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to hardcoded `10.megabytes`. WHY: Lets a remote URL force the server (SSRF-adjacent sink `FileHelper.download`) to fetch/store up to 10MB even when admin capped images much lower, bypassing admin limit and amplifying bandwidth/disk exhaustion via API uploads. HOW: Restore `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` cap (or max(configured, downsizable ceiling)) for the download.

WHAT: In-request `while attempt>0` loop runs up to 5 synchronous `OptimizedImage.downsize` (ImageMagick `convert` + `ImageOptim`) in-place (`tempfile.path` as both from and to) without checking return value. WHY: Each upload of a large image blocks the Rails request on up to 5 expensive convert/optimize passes, and in-place same-path convert risks truncating input before read; attacker-supplied large images cause CPU/latency blowup per request. HOW: Run downsize once with success check/off-request job, use separate temp output file then atomically replace, and break on failure.

WHAT: Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is discarded and loop never breaks on failure. WHY: Failed convert (bad input, corrupt image, convert error) leaves tempfile oversized or truncated, so the loop wastes remaining attempts and Upload.create_for proceeds with an oversized/corrupted file instead of surfacing the failure. HOW: Check the boolean result and break/return error on false instead of retrying on size alone.

feature-can-edit-category-host-relations.texto: WHAT: before_validation calls self.host.sub! without a nil/blank guard. WHY: creating/updating with missing host raises NoMethodError instead of a validation error, 500ing Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host. HOW: guard with `if self.host.present?` before stripping scheme/path.

WHAT: update/destroy use EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first then call save_host(host)/host.destroy without a not-found check. WHY: unknown id passes nil into save_host (nil.host=) or nil.destroy, raising NoMethodError 500 instead of 404. HOW: return 404 when host is nil.

WHAT: save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host]/[:category_id] with no require/presence check. WHY: missing or malformed embeddable_host param raises NoMethodError on nil instead of 400/validation error. HOW: use params.require(:embeddable_host) with permitted keys and handle missing values.

WHAT: record_for_host queries where("lower(host) = ?", host) without downcasing the input, and returns false instead of nil. WHY: uppercase/mixed-case referer hosts (URI#host preserves case) never match, so host_allowed? wrongly rejects legitimate embeds; false vs nil also breaks nil-contract callers. HOW: compare against host.downcase and return nil when not found/parsable.

WHAT: expandable_first_post? dropped the embeddable-hosts-present check and now only checks embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?. WHY: returns true for truncated embeds even when the embeddable_hosts table is empty, re-enabling expansion with no allowed hosts (old spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' now passes vacuously). HOW: also require EmbeddableHost.exists? (or equivalent).

WHAT: migration interpolates raw site_settings value h directly into INSERT string ('#{h}'). WHY: a stored host containing a quote breaks the migration and gives SQL injection from an admin-controlled setting value into schema-migration SQL. HOW: quote/sanitize values or insert via parameterized exec / model create.

WHAT: migration does execute(...)[0]['id']/['value'] assuming rows for embed_category and uncategorized_category_id exist. WHY: on fresh installs or when those settings are absent [0] is nil, so nil['id'] raises and the migration fails. HOW: handle empty results with a fallback/default before to_i.

WHAT: eh = record_for_host(url) can be nil/false (host deleted or normalization mismatch) and category: eh.try(:category_id) then passes nil, unlike the controller fallback to uncategorized_category_id. WHY: PostCreator receives nil category for an embed that passed earlier checks, creating miscategorized or failed topics. HOW: fall back to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id when eh/category is blank.

WHAT: plural branch calls obj[k].map(...) assuming *_ids is always an array. WHY: a null/undefined/singleton ids payload throws TypeError and breaks hydration for that record. HOW: guard Array.isArray(obj[k]) before mapping, defaulting to [].

feature-localization-fallbacks-server-si.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym without nil guard, crashing when default_locale is nil/unloaded. WHY: The PR description itself states default_locale is not guaranteed loaded at boot, so the first fallback resolution raises NoMethodError on nil instead of falling back to :en. HOW: Use SiteSetting.default_locale.try(:to_sym) / safe navigation so compact can drop nil.

WHAT: ensure_loaded! is only wired in the web-request set_locale path, while fallbacks affect every translate (PostAlerter I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale), Jobs::Base I18n.locale= path). WHY: Background/mailers resolve fallback chains to locales never loaded, returning missing translations despite the fallback feature. HOW: Call FallbackLocaleList ensure/preload in those non-request paths or make load_locale lazy-safe for fallback locales.

WHAT: New I18n.ensure_loaded! forwards attacker-influenced locale (User#effective_locale -> self.locale, unchecked) into load_locale which builds Regexp.new("\\.#{locale}\\.yml$") without escaping. WHY: A locale containing regex metacharacters (e.g. ".*") changes which load_path entries match and get loaded, enabling load amplification / ReDoS via crafted profile locale. HOW: Escape with Regexp.escape(locale.to_s) and validate locale against LocaleSiteSetting.supported_locales before loading.

WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] performs a SiteSetting.default_locale lookup on every fallback resolution. WHY: With fallbacks enabled the backend consults fallbacks[locale] per translate/miss, turning hundreds of per-request translates into hundreds of settings lookups and slowing the hot translation path. HOW: Memoize/cache default_locale per request or compute fallback chain once per locale change instead of per key.

fix-concurrent-group-access-to-prevent-n.texto: WHAT: getSubGroupsCount now returns null when the delegate is gone, violating GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() contract documented as Never returns null. WHY: callers expecting non-null Long can NPE on unboxing or misbehave (count shown as unknown vs 0), turning a fixed NPE into a downstream null-dereference. HOW: return a non-null sentinel (e.g. 0L) or throw/handle deleted-group at caller instead of leaking null.

WHAT: reader thread is started with new Thread(...).start() and never joined before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. WHY: assertion races with an in-flight request and the leaked thread keeps hitting the server after the test, so failures after the assert are missed and later tests are polluted — flaky/false-passing test. HOW: keep the Thread reference, join it (with timeout) after deletedAll.set(true) before asserting.

WHAT: reader thread tight-loops groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true) with no sleep/backoff while deletes run. WHY: each iteration requests unbounded full top-level group list, hammering server/DB in a hot spin and slowing the suite. HOW: page with a bounded maxResults and add a small sleep/yield or iteration cap.

fix-handle-collective-multiple-host-on-d.texto: WHAT: mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration dereferences possibly-undefined after array destructuring. WHY: crashes with TypeError when destinationCalendar is null/undefined/[] (all now allowed), breaking booking creation where old `?.integration` was safe. HOW: use mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar" or guard for missing calendar.

WHAT: updateEvent fallback `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is taken only when externalCalendarId is falsy so it can never match. WHY: selectedCalendar becomes undefined and google update is called with undefined calendarId, breaking updates; old code fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId.

WHAT: deleteEvent has the same dead fallback `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` in the else-branch. WHY: when externalCalendarId is absent the lookup compares against undefined and always yields undefined, so deletes fall back to "primary" instead of the stored destination calendar.

WHAT: evt.destinationCalendar initialized to null when no organizer/event-type calendar, then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently no-ops. WHY: collective team destination calendars are dropped and multi-host invites/DB connect lose hosts; other call sites use []. HOW: initialize to [] instead of null.

WHAT: no-credentialId branch calls createEvent(c, event) without destination.externalId while references now use result.externalId. WHY: externalCalendarId is lost (undefined) for those bookings whereas old code used evt.destinationCalendar.externalId. HOW: pass destination.externalId through.

WHAT: createEvent always uses destinationCalendar[0] and ignores the per-destination credentialId/externalId that EventManager now loops over. WHY: for collective multi-host bookings every iteration creates on the main host calendar (duplicates/wrong target) instead of the matching host calendar like Google does.

WHAT: createEvent/createAttendees/updateEvent/deleteEvent always use destinationCalendar[0] and ignore credentialId/externalId. WHY: collective second-host iterations operate on the main host calendarId, creating/updating/deleting the wrong calendar.

WHAT: slug spread condition inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && {slug}` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {slug} : {}`. WHY: organizations get/miss slug in the opposite billing mode, breaking org creation/slug uniqueness vs prior behavior.

WHAT: createAllCalendarEvents awaits prisma.credential.findUnique and createEvent sequentially inside for-of over destinations. WHY: N destinations cause N sequential DB round-trips plus N sequential calendar API calls instead of batched/parallel, growing latency with team size.

WHAT: Booking create persists only evt.destinationCalendar[0].id while creation fans out to all evt.destinationCalendar entries. WHY: Reschedule/cancel/reject reload booking.destinationCalendar (single FK) so events created on co-hosts' calendars are never updated/deleted, leaving orphan calendar events and inconsistent state. HOW: Persist all destinations (e.g. join table or store each createdEvent externalId/credentialId reference) instead of connecting only the first entry.

fix-proper-handling-of-group-memberships.texto: WHAT: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 which is off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100/50 yields 3 instead of 2) and yields 1 for 0 handled separately but 2 for exactly one page. WHY: next clamps to user_count so UI navigates to an empty trailing page (offset == total) with currentPage == totalPages showing empty members. HOW: use Math.ceil(user_count / limit), e.g. Math.ceil(this.get(user_count)/this.get(limit)).

WHAT: add_members splits usernames on comma without stripping whitespace, so 'user1, user2' looks up ' user2' via User.find_by_username and silently skips it. WHY: user-selector input joins with commas/spaces so the second and later usernames fail to be added with no error. HOW: strip each token (username.strip or username.strip!) before lookup and skip blanks.

WHAT: members action takes user-controlled limit/offset with no cap or validation (limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i). WHY: attacker can request limit=1000000 to force order+limit huge member serialization in one request, causing memory/CPU blowup on large groups. HOW: clamp limit to a max (e.g. min(limit, 200)) and sanitize negative/zero values.

WHAT: remove_member automatic-group test issues xhr :put while routes.rb maps remove_member to DELETE and add_members to PUT. WHY: controller-action spec bypasses routing so it never verifies the DELETE route wiring and gives false confidence the guard is reachable via the real verb. HOW: change to xhr :delete, :remove_member to match config/routes.rb.

WHAT: add_members/remove_member read params.require(:group_id) but the routes define member routes (/admin/groups/:id/members) so the id arrives as params[:id], not params[:group_id]. WHY: Real requests from group.js (`/admin/groups/:id/members.json`) raise ActionController::ParameterMissing and member add/remove is broken; specs pass only because they inject group_id directly bypassing routing. HOW: Read the id the route provides (e.g. Group.find(params[:id] || params[:group_id])) or declare the routes as collection/with explicit :group_id segment.

fixing-re-authentication-with-passkeys-k.texto: WHAT: setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError sets USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED on a throwaway LoginFormsProvider from context.form() that is never rendered. WHY: context.form() creates a new provider per call (AuthenticationProcessor.java:589-612), and both callers render with a different instance — WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse uses at least 3 distinct context.form() calls (setError, setup, fillContextForm, errorChallenge) and badPasswordHandler renders via challenge() with a fresh instance — so after a passkey/password error during re-auth the flags are lost, falling back to editable-username regular login. HOW: Set the attributes on the same provider instance used to render (e.g., return/pass the form or set them after fillContextForm inside the rendering path).

frontend-asset-optimization-grafana-code.texto: WHAT: Write lock is acquired at line 48 without re-checking the cache and is held across blocking file/CDN I/O. WHY: Concurrent cache misses that all passed the RLock check serialize on the exclusive lock and each redoes manifest file/network reads, while concurrent cache-hit readers needing RLock block for the full I/O duration. HOW: Re-check entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock and return early on hit, and only hold the lock for publishing the pointer (do I/O outside the lock or use singleflight).

github-oauth-security-enhancement-sentry.texto: WHAT: OAuth state uses pipeline.signature which is a deterministic md5 of pipeline view class names, identical for every user/org. WHY: Attacker knows the state value (open-source class names) and can forge setup?code=attacker_code&state=known-value to mount OAuth login-CSRF / code-substitution, defeating the state mismatch check the PR claims to add.

WHAT: safe_urlopen token exchange and get_user_info (which calls raise_for_status) are not wrapped in try/except, unlike the payload parse below them. WHY: Any non-2xx, timeout, or network error from GitHub raises and returns 500 instead of the intended error page, breaking the install flow on transient failures.

WHAT: Direct access integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] assumes sender always present. WHY: Legacy integrations and build_integration paths where state lacked sender (integration.py:376-377, installation.py:44 explicitly handles missing sender) raise KeyError and 500 instead of the error page when re-installing such an integration.

WHAT: The new github_authenticated_user vs sender[login] check only runs when the Integration row already exists, while the Integration.DoesNotExist path returns pipeline.next_step() with no verification. WHY: GitHub installation webhooks arrive asynchronously, so completing the pipeline before the webhook creates the Integration bypasses the intended installer-identity check and defeats the security control. HOW: Do not advance on DoesNotExist; either fail closed with error() or verify the installer via live GitHub API (get_installation_info) instead of only the DB row.

implement-access-token-context-encoding-.texto: WHAT: Constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType) twice and never validates rawTokenId (second message even says rawTokenId). WHY: A null rawTokenId passes construction and later produces a malformed encoded id (':null' suffix) or NPE downstream instead of failing fast. HOW: Change line 73 to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

WHAT: isAccessTokenId uses inverted logic `if (substring(3,5).equals(expected)) return false` with off-by-one offset (grant occupies chars 4-6, not 3-5). WHY: Matcher rejects correct grant shortcuts and accepts wrong ones (plus checks wrong slice), making code-to-token/refresh/device/CIBA assertions false-positive/negative. HOW: Guard length and use `if (!items[0].substring(4,6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

WHAT: Context caches grantType at construction from formParams but setFormParams() replaces formParams without refreshing the cached grantType. WHY: Any caller mutating form params leaves getGrantType() stale, so OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse stores the wrong Constants.GRANT_TYPE and the token-id prefix encodes the wrong grant. HOW: Update grantType inside setFormParams (or compute getGrantType() lazily from current formParams).

WHAT: New interface method String getShortcut() has no default implementation. WHY: Every existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory breaks at runtime/compile (AbstractMethodError) and DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit NPEs on null (ConcurrentHashMap forbids null), crashing startup. HOW: Provide a default e.g. `default String getShortcut() { return DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.UNKNOWN; }` and null-validate in postInit.

WHAT: initToken unconditionally dereferences session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class) and encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException for unknown grantType. WHY: Token issuance that previously always succeeded with a UUID now fails with NPE (provider missing) or 500 (unregistered/custom grant string from formParams) for flows that never set a mapped GRANT_TYPE. HOW: Fall back to KeycloakModelUtils.generateId() when encoder is null or shortcut is unknown.

notification-rule-processing-engine-graf.texto: WHAT: Grafana branch of FilterViewResults renders GrafanaRuleListItem without key={key} while datasource and unknown branches pass it. WHY: Breaks the artificial frontend key used to prevent duplication and causes wrong reconciliation/remounts during infinite-scroll pagination. HOW: Add key={key} to the GrafanaRuleListItem element.

WHAT: Pause/Delete/Duplicate/Silence/Export permissions are OR-combined between ruler abilities and new grafana prom abilities, while provisioned detection for prom path depends on optional promRule.provenance. WHY: If prom DTO omits provenance, isProvisionedPromRule is false so the grafana side reports editable/removable and the OR grants Edit/Delete/Pause on provisioned immutable rules that the ruler path would deny. HOW: Require both sides to agree on immutability or fall back to denied when provenance is unknown.

WHAT: Loader now renders only promResponse groups and dropped the ruler query plus matchRules Creating/Deleting branches. WHY: Ruler-only (newly creating) rules disappear from the list and prom-only (deleting) rules now render as normal editable rules with Edit/More instead of Deleting placeholders. HOW: Restore ruler fetch with matchRules or explicitly handle creating/deleting states from prom-only data.

WHAT: GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule to RuleActionsButtons, leaving rulerRule undefined, but the silence drawer still gates on rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule). WHY: Clicking Silence from the list-view menu sets showSilenceDrawer with no rulerRule so the drawer never opens and the action silently does nothing. HOW: Wire SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer to promRule or hide/disable the silence action when only promRule is available.

WHAT: useAllRulerRuleAbilities hardcodes isFederated=false (TODO) after refactor dropped the isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check. WHY: Federated Mimir ruler rules are no longer treated as immutable, so Update/Delete/Pause/Restore wrongly appear supported and editable for rules that cannot be edited. HOW: Thread the group through (or resolve federated status from groupIdentifier) and restore the isFederatedRuleGroup guard in the immutableRule computation.

oauth-credential-sync-and-app-integratio.texto: WHAT: Credential update stores the whole Zod SafeParse result ({success,data}) as key instead of parsed data. WHY: Next googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) will fail and all Google calendar calls break after one refresh when sync is enabled. HOW: Store key.data (or parsed value) instead of the wrapper.

WHAT: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] which do not match arbitrary fields, so safeParse strips refresh_token/expiry, then code injects refresh_token='refresh_token' literal. WHY: Merging this data overwrites the real refresh_token with a dummy string and drops expiry/instance_url, permanently breaking future refreshes. HOW: Define minimum schema with access_token plus optional passthrough fields and preserve existing refresh_token instead of dummy.

WHAT: Sync path returns raw fetch Response while callers expect provider shapes (Google expects res.data, axios callers expect tokenInfo.data). WHY: Google does token.access_token on undefined and Bigin/Zoho do tokenInfo.data.error on undefined, throwing TypeError on every synced refresh. HOW: Parse the sync response (response.json()) and normalize to the shape each caller expects or branch per caller.

WHAT: refreshOAuthTokens is called with credentialId (credential.id) as the userId argument. WHY: Remote sync endpoint receives credentialId as calcomUserId, looks up the wrong user, and team credentials incorrectly take the sync path since id is always truthy. HOW: Pass credential.userId (and guard team/null) instead of credentialId.

WHAT: JSON.parse(req.query.state) throws on attacker-controlled malformed state with no try/catch. WHY: Any crafted /api/integrations/*/callback?state=not-json crashes the handler with 500 instead of 400. HOW: Wrap in try/catch and return undefined or throw HttpError 400.

WHAT: New jsforce.Connection uses stale credentialKey.access_token/instance_url instead of the freshly refreshed accessTokenParsed.data. WHY: Refresh is fetched and persisted but never used, so calls continue with the expired token. HOW: Use accessTokenParsed.data.access_token (and instance_url) for the new connection.

WHAT: Error check uses response.statusText !== 'OK' instead of response.ok/status. WHY: statusText is empty/unreliable in node-fetch/undici, causing false failures or missed HTTP errors on Salesforce refresh. HOW: Check !response.ok or status code range.

WHAT: Team credential creation only checks accepted membership, not admin role, while non-team path enforces throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam. WHY: Any accepted team member can mint team-level OAuth credentials by crafting state.teamId, escalating to team-wide integration access. HOW: Require admin/owner check for teamId path too.

WHAT: Decrypted keys are JSON.parse'd with no schema validation and written directly to credential.key for arbitrary userId/appSlug. WHY: Holder of the shared webhook secret (or leaked secret) can inject malformed credential JSON that later crashes schema parses or hijacks integrations for any user. HOW: Validate keys against per-app credential schema before create/update and reject on mismatch.

WHAT: Sync fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout/AbortSignal, no error handling, and runs in the hot token-refresh path for every calendar/video call. WHY: A slow or down sync endpoint blocks availability/booking flows until default fetch timeout, causing material latency blowup per request. HOW: Add AbortSignal.timeout and fall back to refreshFunction on failure.

WHAT: appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) throws unhandled ZodError on malformed body with no try/catch. WHY: Any request with missing/invalid userId/appSlug/keys crashes the handler with 500 instead of returning 400, breaking error contract and leaking exception path. HOW: Use safeParse and return 400 on failure.

WHAT: Missing refresh_token is replaced with literal placeholder string "refresh_token" and persisted. WHY: Stored credential gets a fake refresh_token so the next refresh sends an invalid token and permanently breaks renewal for that user. HOW: Preserve the existing stored refresh_token or leave the field absent instead of injecting a placeholder.

optimize-header-layout-performance-with-.texto: WHAT: order() passes $val unchanged to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group, which are 1-indexed while order is 0-indexed. WHY: @include order(2)/order(3) in topic.scss/header.scss render one position off on legacy -webkit-box/-moz-box browsers, misordering header panel vs extra-info. HOW: add 1 for the old box model, e.g. -webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1.

WHAT: align-items() emits -ms-align-items: $alignment which is a non-existent property (IE10 uses only -ms-flex-align). WHY: the declaration is dead code so IE10/IE11-legacy alignment relies solely on -ms-flex-align, and future flex-start/flex-end values would pass through untranslated and fail. HOW: drop the -ms-align-items line and map flex-start/flex-end to start/end for -ms-flex-align.

plugins-chore-renamed-instrumentation-mi.texto: WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware reuses a single shared *MetricsMiddleware and mutates imw.next on every CreateClientMiddleware call. WHY: Decorator.clientFromMiddlewares rebuilds the chain per request, so concurrent requests concurrently write/read imw.next causing a data race and potentially routing through another request's downstream chain. HOW: Allocate a new MetricsMiddleware per call (copy pluginMetrics/registry, set next) like ContextualLoggerMiddleware/LoggerMiddleware do.

WHAT: logRequest dropped explicit pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname/traceID fields and now relies solely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx). WHY: Those fields only appear if upstream NewContextualLoggerMiddleware ran and global contextual/trace providers are registered, so standalone use or reordering of LoggerMiddleware silently loses plugin/request identity in logs. HOW: Keep explicit fields or document/enforce the ordering dependency.

WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext ignores the receiver and returns a fresh NewTestLogger(). WHY: Calls like m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info in LoggerMiddleware record on a throwaway logger, so assertions on the injected fake see zero calls and context/state is lost unlike the real wrapper which derives from the receiver. HOW: Return the receiver (or a derived copy sharing its capture) instead of a new instance.

replays-self-serve-bulk-delete-system-se.texto: WHAT: fetch_error_details pairs IDs to payloads with zip(error_ids, events.values()) instead of key lookup. WHY: get_multi dict order is not guaranteed to match error_ids order, so titles/messages/timestamps attach to the wrong error id and chronological merge is corrupted. HOW: map via node_ids, e.g. lookup events[node_id] per error_id.

WHAT: validate_timestamp/validate_age use truthiness self.initial_data.get(age/timestamp) so age=0 or timestamp=0 bypass mutual-exclusion. WHY: a report containing both age and timestamp with a zero value incorrectly validates, breaking Working-Draft vs Editors-Draft exclusivity. HOW: check key presence (e.g. in self.initial_data) instead of truthiness.

WHAT: use-table-widget-visualization branch renders hardcoded empty columns={[]} and tableData {data:[],meta:{fields:{},units:{}}} ignoring result/data/meta. WHY: dashboards show an empty table with no columns instead of real query results when flag is on; [] also suppresses the columns fallback. HOW: pass through actual result data/meta and derived columns.

WHAT: attacker-influenced environment.name and issue title are interpolated unsanitized into PR-comment markdown. WHY: environment comes from event data and title from issue data; backticks/brackets/parentheses break the [**title**](url) template and let an attacker inject markdown/links into bot-posted GitHub/GitLab comments. HOW: escape/sanitize markdown special chars in title and environment before formatting.

WHAT: unauthenticated endpoint loops over unbounded raw_data array running full serializer validation per report with no length cap. WHY: an attacker can POST a huge array to permission_classes=() endpoint causing CPU/memory blowup per request. HOW: enforce a max batch size (e.g. reject >N reports with 422/413).

WHAT: Fallback columnOrder does Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields) which throws when tableData is undefined/null (tableData?.meta evaluates to undefined then .fields access throws) or when meta.fields is undefined. WHY: Crashes table render on empty/loading data instead of rendering empty table, breaking the empty-data story the component explicitly supports. HOW: Use Object.keys(tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {}) to safely fallback to empty columns.

WHAT: useQuery queryKey is ['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions] with no organization identifier while fetcher closes over organization.slug. WHY: Switching organizations with identical datetime/projects/type reuses the previous org's cached TagCollection, showing wrong attribute keys cross-org until refetch. HOW: Include organization.slug (or selection-dependent org key) in the queryKey.

sms-workflow-reminder-retry-count-tracki.texto: WHAT: The second OR branch (retryCount gt 1) has no method/scheduled/scheduledDate filter, so it deletes every WorkflowReminder with retryCount>1. WHY: Successfully scheduled SMS rows keep their retryCount (success path never resets it) and non-SMS rows share the same table, so this deletes live/scheduled reminders, loses referenceId and orphans Twilio jobs. HOW: Scope the branch to method SMS and scheduled:false.

WHAT: Failure increment uses stale read reminder.retryCount + 1 instead of an atomic increment. WHY: Overlapping cron executions read the same value and both write the same +1, losing a retry and delaying/preventing the retryCount>1 deletion. HOW: Use data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }.
WHAT: The catch-block increment also uses stale reminder.retryCount + 1. WHY: Same lost-update race as the else branch — concurrent failures undercount retries. HOW: Use atomic increment.

WHAT: When message is empty or sendTo is falsy the if(message?.length && sendTo) guard fails and neither the scheduled update nor the else retryCount increment runs. WHY: Reminders with missing smsReminderNumber/empty body are refetched every cron run for up to 7 days with no retry counting, preserving the infinite-retry loop this PR claims to fix. HOW: Add an else that increments retryCount (or marks/cancels the reminder) when message/sendTo is missing.

WHAT: deleteMany filters on retryCount gt 1 but schema has no index on retryCount (only bookingUid, workflowStepId, seatReferenceId, [method,scheduled,scheduledDate]). WHY: Every cron tick runs an unindexed predicate over the whole WorkflowReminder table, forcing a full scan as the table grows. HOW: Scope the delete to indexed columns and/or add @@index([retryCount]) or [method, scheduled, retryCount].

WHAT: The newly added await prisma.workflowReminder.update inside the catch block can itself throw and abort the whole batch. WHY: A single failing retry-count write (e.g. P2025 after a concurrent cron deleted the row, or a transient DB error) escapes the for loop, skips all remaining reminders and skips the final res.json, turning one bad row into a failed cron tick. HOW: Guard the catch-block write with its own nested try/catch (log and continue) so bookkeeping failures never abort scheduling of the remaining reminders.

span-buffer-multiprocess-enhancement-wit.texto: WHAT: isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is always False for spawn-context processes so kill() on restart (and terminate() in join) never runs. WHY: hung/crashed flusher is replaced while the old spawn process keeps flushing the same shards, causing duplicate Kafka produces, races in done_flush_segments, and zombie-process leaks. HOW: check against the spawn context type (e.g. self.mp_context.Process / BaseProcess) or call kill/terminate without the false guard; same pattern at join lines 346-347.

WHAT: join() computes remaining_time but never uses it and breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires. WHY: after next_step.join(timeout) consumes the budget the first expired deadline skips waiting/terminating all remaining flusher processes, leaving them running/leaked on shutdown and defeating the timeout contract. HOW: divide the remaining budget per process or track per-process deadlines and still terminate unwaited processes.

WHAT: submit() fans cluster-wide Redis work out per shard-buffer (N pipelines for record_stored_segments plus N full iter_cluster_memory_usage scans summed at lines 299-301). WHY: per-message Redis round trips and cluster memory scans grow O(num_processes) on the submit hot path instead of one pipeline/scan, multiplying Redis load as flusher processes scale. HOW: keep a single pipeline/scan over all shards or cache memory info out of the per-message path.

unified-storage-performance-optimization.texto: WHAT: BuildIndex no longer serializes whole builds — only the final cache write at b.cache[key]=idx is locked, so concurrent builds for the same key run fully in parallel. WHY: Two goroutines building the same NamespacedResource both call bleve.New on the same dir (filepath.Join(Root,Namespace,Resource.Group)) and both run ListIterator+Write+Flush, causing duplicate work, file-handle/dir contention and last-wins cache clobbering with double IndexTenants.Inc. HOW: Restore per-key mutual exclusion (singleflight or per-key lock) around the build, keeping the fine-grained cache lock only for the map write.

WHAT: NewResourceServer calls s.Init(ctx) but on error returns nil,err without invoking s.cancel (or Stop), leaking the cancellable watcher context and any partially started lifecycle/search watch resources. WHY: Failed construction leaves the context.Background-derived s.ctx and its goroutines (broadcaster/search watch) uncancelled with no handle to clean up, leaking resources on every failed startup/index-build attempt. HOW: On Init error call s.cancel() (or defer cleanup) before returning nil,err.
